name: Solenoid MOSFET driver (Adafruit 5648) with 5 V solenoid
description: Low-side N-channel MOSFET switch with an on-board flyback diode, used to fire a 5 V push-pull solenoid from a 3.3 V or 5 V GPIO: the In signal drives the gate of an AO3406 MOSFET (30 V, 70 mOhm max at VGS 4.5 V, VGS(th) 1.5-2.5 V) directly, with a 10 kOhm pull-down (red Sig LED also fed from In through 10 kOhm); a 1N400x / SM4002 diode across the + / - terminal block clamps the coil's turn-off spike. Power V+ 3-30 V, logic 2.5-20 V, 1.5 A continuous / 3 A peak. The usual load is the Adafruit 2776 mini push-pull solenoid (5 V, 4.5 Ohm, 1.1 A, 3 mm stroke), fed from its own 5 V supply. Sold as: Adafruit STEMMA MOSFET+Diode Driver (product 5648, 0.1 inch header Out, In, V+, GND; JST PH V+/GND/In; 2-way terminal block + / -), typically paired with the Adafruit Mini Push-Pull Solenoid - 5V (product 2776).
eli5: An electronic switch with a built-in spike catcher: your board's small signal lets a big 1 A current flow through the solenoid so its plunger snaps in.

pins.name: Out
pins.description: Switched output = terminal block '-': the MOSFET drain, pulled to GND while In is high. Solenoid's second lead goes here (or on the '-' screw terminal). Never wire it to a GPIO.

pins.name: In
pins.description: Signal input (gate), active high, 2.5-20 V: high = solenoid on, low or unconnected = off (10 kOhm pull-down on the board). A 3.3 V GPIO is enough for a 1 A solenoid. PWM works for holding at lower power.

pins.name: V+
pins.description: Load power = terminal block '+'. The driver board accepts 3-30 V, but here it feeds the 5 V solenoid, so it must be a separate regulated 5 V supply (at least 1.5 A for the Adafruit 2776's 1.1 A), not the microcontroller's 3V3/5V pin. Solenoid's first lead goes on '+'.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Common ground for the load supply and the microcontroller (MOSFET source).

supplierQuery: Adafruit 5648 STEMMA MOSFET Diode Driver + Adafruit 2776 mini push-pull solenoid 5V
buildNotes: Two current paths share one ground: In and GND go to the microcontroller; the solenoid sits on the terminal block between '+' (= V+) and '-' (= Out). Feed V+ from a separate 5 V supply (1.5 A or more) and join its ground to the board's GND.
Do not power a 1.1 A solenoid from the microcontroller board's 5V/VBUS pin or a computer USB port: the inrush browns out the board.
The flyback diode is already on the board, across + and -, so no extra diode is needed. Solenoid polarity does not matter.
Use short pulses. A small 5 V push-pull solenoid gets hot if held on: pulse it (e.g. 50 ms-1 s) or, to hold, pull in at full power and then drop to about 30-50 % PWM duty.
V+ here must be 5 V to match the 5 V solenoid (the driver board itself accepts 3-30 V, so a higher supply is only for a solenoid rated for it): a 5 V solenoid on 12 V will overheat quickly.
Rated 1.5 A continuous, 3 A peak (AO3406 in SOT-23, no heatsink). The JST PH connector is rated only 2 A; use the terminal block for the load.
The red Sig LED shows the input state; the green ON LED shows V+ is present. Each can be disabled by cutting its jumper on the back.

example.code:
from machine import Pin
import time

solenoid = Pin({IN}, Pin.OUT, value=0)  # In high = MOSFET on = solenoid pulls in
while True:
    solenoid.value(1)
    print('SOLENOID ON')
    time.sleep(1)   # short pulse: the 5 V solenoid is not rated for continuous duty
    solenoid.value(0)
    print('SOLENOID OFF')
    time.sleep(2)
